items.followUp: State the main feature of Dobereiner’s triads and give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining grouping and shared properties of a triad.
rubric.description: Some elements were arranged in groups of three with similar chemical properties
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Dobereiner grouped elements in threes with similar chemical properties.

rubric.why: States the approximate relationship between the atomic masses in a triad.
rubric.description: The middle element’s atomic mass is approximately the arithmetic mean of the other two
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the middle element’s atomic mass as approximately the arithmetic mean of the other two.

modelAnswer: Dobereiner arranged some elements in groups of three, called triads, whose elements had similar chemical properties.
The atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of the other two elements.
For example, Li, Na and K form a triad.

items.followUp: Explain why atomic size decreases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Recognizes that the number of occupied shells increases down a group.
rubric.description: Each successive element down a group has an additional occupied electron shell
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an additional occupied shell is added down a group.

rubric.why: Connects the increased distance of the outermost electrons to the increase in atomic radius.
rubric.description: The outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus, so atomic radius increases
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus and the atomic radius consequently increases.

modelAnswer: Down a group, each successive element has an additional occupied electron shell.
Therefore, the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus and the atomic radius increases.

items.followUp: Identify the type of covalent bond in O₂ and N₂.

rubric.why: Identifies the bonding in methane correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the C–H bonds in CH₄ as single covalent bonds.

rubric.why: Identifies the bonding in ethane correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the C–C and C–H bonds in C₂H₆ as single covalent bonds.

modelAnswer: CH₄ contains four single covalent C–H bonds.
C₂H₆ contains a single covalent C–C bond and single covalent C–H bonds.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for chlorine reacting with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: Identifies all the products formed in the reaction.
rubric.description: The products are sodium chloride, sodium chlorate and water
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving all three products: NaCl, NaClO₃ and H₂O.

rubric.why: Gives the balanced equation and the stated reaction conditions.
rubric.description: Balanced equation for chlorine with hot, concentrated NaOH
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation with hot, concentrated sodium hydroxide.
